text:
ira-customer: Hey team, our Private deployment behind an NLB shows target group instances unhealthy. Apps return 200 internally but ALB/NLB health checks are timing out, causing 503s for traffic. CI is failing. Anyone seen this pattern?
jess-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the target group health check settings + example failing IP:port?
ira-customer: Health check: protocol=HTTP path=/healthz port=8443 interval=10s timeout=5s healthy=3 unhealthy=2. Targets marked unhealthy -> reason: Connection timed out. Example target ip 10.0.5.23:8443
matt-sre: Quick checklist: 1) Is TLS terminated at the LB or at Envoy? 2) Do health checks include SNI or client certs? 3) Security group/NACL allowing health check source IPs?
ira-customer: TLS is terminated at Envoy (backend). We use mTLS for front-door -> envoy, and Envoy expects client certs. Health checks come from the NLB and don't present client certs. We suspected that might be it.
jess-support: That aligns — if Envoy requires client certs, plain HTTP/S health checks from the LB will fail. Two options: terminate TLS at ALB/NLB and forward plain HTTP to Envoy health endpoint, or expose an unauthenticated health path on the pod for the LB to hit.
matt-sre: Also confirm NLB health check type: NLB TCP checks won't send SNI or HTTP headers. If you're using HTTP health check on NLB but backend expects TLS handshake with SNI+client certs, it will time out. For ALB, the ALB can use HTTPS health checks but still won't attach client certs.
olivia-platform: Quick repro steps your team can run from inside the VPC: 
1) From a bastion in the same subnet: `curl -v --resolve app.example.internal:8443:10.0.5.23 https://app.example.internal:8443/healthz`
2) Test raw TLS handshake: `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.23:8443 -servername app.example.internal`
If s_client stalls or returns "no peer certificate" issues, it's a TLS handshake problem.
ira-customer: Ran both: `curl` hangs, `openssl s_client` shows TLS handshake but then Envoy closes because client cert missing: "alert unknown ca" in logs.
jess-support: That log confirms mTLS is the cause. For immediate mitigation you can: 
- Create a dedicated TCP target group + NLB health check on a plain HTTP port (eg. 8080) that Envoy listens on without mTLS, or
- Configure Envoy to accept a specific health endpoint with `allow_no_client_cert` and return 200, or
- Terminate TLS at the LB (ALB) and forward HTTP to Envoy (less preferred if you need mTLS end-to-end).
matt-sre: Also double-check security groups: NLB uses the node's ENI and source IP of health checks will be from the subnet. If you have restrictive SGs only allowing 10.0.0.0/16, make sure the health-check source addresses are permitted. For private deployments there are no AWS-managed health IP ranges like public ALBs, so source will be within your VPC.
jess-support: FYI for customers that use egress allowlists: our platform's control plane may perform probes for provisioning; ensure your egress allowlist includes our control plane FQDNs (redwood-internal.example.com) or the IP ranges we provided in onboarding. But in this case sounds internal only.
ira-customer: We can expose a plain HTTP /_redwood_probe on 9001 that bypasses auth. Would you recommend that?
matt-sre: Yes, expose an internal-only health endpoint bound to 127.0.0.1 or pod IP and open SG from NLB -> target port 9001. Then point the target group health check to /_redwood_probe on 9001 with HTTP. That avoids mTLS issues and keeps public traffic mTLS enforced.
olivia-platform: Example target group health config we recommend for ALB (HTTPS backend with termination at ALB): `protocol=HTTP, path=/healthz, port=9001, matcher=200-399, interval=10, timeout=5` For NLB + TCP health checks use `protocol=TCP, port=9001` but ensure Envoy listens plain TCP on that port.
jess-support: Quick commands to validate from your bastion: 
- `nc -vz 10.0.5.23 9001` (check TCP reachability)
- `curl -sS http://10.0.5.23:9001/_redwood_probe -I` (expect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`)
- `kubectl logs deploy/envoy -n prod | grep health` (look for health endpoint hits)
let us know outputs and we can confirm target group will mark healthy.
ira-customer: Ran `nc` -> succeeded. `curl` returns 200. Envoy logs show `GET /_redwood_probe` hits. After I updated target group to port 9001 health checks now PASS. Back to normal. Thanks. :tada:
jess-support: Awesome — closing loop: root cause = Envoy mTLS required client certs so LB health checks (no client cert) timed out. Remediation = add unauthenticated internal health endpoint or change LB termination to provide certs (not typical).
matt-sre: I'll add a short KB note we can share with other customers: "NLB/ALB health checks and mTLS backends" with recommended patterns. Assigning to @matt-sre to draft.
deploy-bot: deploy status: kb/nlb-mtls-healthchecks-draft #21 -> in progress
ira-customer: Appreciate the quick help — will monitor for an hour then close the ticket.
jess-support: Thanks — ping us if it reoccurs, we can inspect target group metrics and Envoy logs further.
